topics.notes: Asset/threat/vulnerability/residual-risk distinction and separate positive/negative operations reviewed; no zero-risk claim.
Disclosure, unauthorized alteration and timely use remain independent; public digest versus trusted reference reviewed.
Listener versus reachable endpoint versus vulnerability separated; no remote scanning/exploitation instructions.
Layer 2 separation differs from routed enforcement; selected tuple and independent return path reviewed.
Prevent/detect/recover and common failure domains separated; no unsupported probability multiplication.
First-match order, wildcard ignored bits, nonempty-list implicit deny, empty/absent consumer exception and stateless limits reviewed.
Source-only semantics and destination-side heuristic limits reviewed; visible destination/port context explicitly ignored.
Transport/destination-port match, NAT observation and fragment exclusions retained; response state never inferred.
Names/sequences and shared consumers reviewed; no new algorithm or statefulness attributed to naming.
Ingress trust bypass distinguished from accepted binding; ARP ACL precedence/rate/header checks remain excluded from model.
Server trust, VLAN scope, binding prerequisite and persistence distinguished from allocation and authenticated identity.
IP-only/IP-and-MAC and attachment scope reviewed; static host address is not a valid switch binding.
Distinct mapped roles and same-community relation reviewed; gateway-routed bypass remains separate.
EAPOL/RADIUS roles, returned policy consumption, MAB exception and protected server trust reviewed.
Accept/reject/unavailable, configured local fallback, command permission and accounting retention kept independent.
Protect/restrict/shutdown effects and accepted/count boundary reviewed; error-disabled target recovery remains guided.
Transit versus CPU punts and service continuity reviewed; no actual CPU/drop prediction from arithmetic.
Pps/bit/s/packet-size conversion, equality boundary and burst/token/accounting exclusions reviewed.
Overlay scope, independent underlay and protected application operation reviewed; no tunnel created by worksheet.
SPD/SAD/selectors, directional SAs, anti-replay and ESP/AH limits reviewed; transform support and execution remain external.
IKEv2 initial exchange/authentication/child-SA distinction, identities and renewal reviewed; no IKEv1 phase labels substituted.
Gateway identities/selectors, protected source route, NAT handling and return/app evidence reviewed independently.
User/device validation, route/DNS/split policy, least privilege and account revocation reviewed.
Packet filtering versus stateful return, NAT and endpoint/application authorization kept distinct.
Directional zone pair and inspect/pass/drop relation reviewed; self/same-zone policy caveats preserved.
ASA 9.20 routed/transparent/context/security-level and NAT/inspection scope reviewed without universal template.
FMC/FTD configuration/deployment, connection decision and intrusion content visibility reviewed; licensing/lifecycle external.
Passive alert versus inline prevention, visibility, false positives and fail-open/closed boundary reviewed.
HTTP-aware deployment, TLS visibility, rule match/tuning and app authorization remain independent; no regex sold as real WAF.
Identity/device/resource/session policy and enforcement separated; location never substitutes for trust.
Attachment/posture/profiling/role consumption and remediation exceptions reviewed; classification is not protected identity.
ISE 3.4 ordered policy-set selection and authentication/authorization/profile consumption reviewed; live logs not end-to-end proof.
Original security scope joins segmentation, allowed/denied operations, identity and independent recovery; loopback fixture is application scope only.
